Follow clusters across time windows

Source: R/merge_dynamic_clusters.R
merge_dynamic_clusters.Rd

When clusters are detected in each time window separately, their identifiers mean nothing from one window to the next: cluster "01" of the 1975-1984 network and cluster "01" of the 1976-1985 network may be two different literatures. merge_dynamic_clusters() links the clusters of successive windows that share most of their nodes, and gives them a common identifier, so that a cluster becomes an entity that can be born, persist and disappear. This is the step that turns a series of networks into a history of research communities, in the spirit of the alluvial maps of Rosvall and Bergstrom (2010) .

Two rules are available, chosen with method. Let \(V_a\) be the nodes of cluster \(a\) in window \(t-1\) and \(V_b\) those of cluster \(b\) in window \(t\).

  • method = "majority", a double majority. Cluster \(b\) inherits the identifier of \(a\) when most nodes of \(a\) go to \(b\) and most nodes of \(b\) come from \(a\): $$\frac{|V_a \cap V_b|}{D_a} > \tau \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{|V_a \cap V_b|}{D_b} > \tau,$$ with \(\tau\) the threshold_similarity, strictly above 0.5. Since \(\tau > 0.5\), a cluster can inherit at most one identifier, and an identifier passes to at most one cluster.

  • method = "jaccard", an overlap matching with a Jaccard threshold, as in the tracking of dynamic communities of Greene et al. (2010) . The Jaccard index of two clusters is the share of their union that they have in common, $$J(a, b) = \frac{|V_a \cap V_b|}{|V_a \cup V_b|}.$$ The pairs with \(J(a, b) \geq \theta\), \(\theta\) being the threshold_similarity, are candidate matches. They are taken one by one, by decreasing \(J\) (then by decreasing number of shared nodes), skipping the pairs where \(a\) or \(b\) has already been matched: each past identifier goes to the present cluster that resembles it most, and each cluster inherits at most one identifier. \(\theta\) can be below 0.5: a cluster that loses a large part of its members to another cluster, or that doubles with newcomers, can keep its identity if it stays the best match of its predecessor.

In both rules, a cluster that meets no match gets a new identifier. The sets \(V\) depend on similarity_type: with "complete", they are all the nodes of the clusters (\(D_a = |V_a|\), \(D_b = |V_b|\)); with "partial", only the nodes present in both windows count (\(D_a = |V_a \cap V_t|\), \(D_b = |V_b \cap V_{t-1}|\), and the union of the Jaccard index is restricted to them), \(V_t\) being all the nodes of window \(t\).

There is no default method, threshold_similarity or similarity_type: they change the dynamic clusters, so the choice must be explicit, and verbose = TRUE reports the rule that is applied.

Usage

merge_dynamic_clusters(
  graphs,
  cluster_id,
  node_id,
  method = c("majority", "jaccard"),
  threshold_similarity,
  similarity_type = c("complete", "partial"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

graphs

A list of at least two tbl_graphs in chronological order (oldest first), as produced by build_dynamic_networks() and add_clusters().

cluster_id

Character scalar, the node column with the clusters of each window (e.g. "cluster_leiden").

node_id

Character scalar, the node column with an identifier that is stable across windows (e.g. "source_id").

method

"majority" (double majority) or "jaccard" (overlap matching with a Jaccard threshold), see the description. Required.

threshold_similarity

The threshold of the rule. For method = "majority", \(\tau\) in \((0.5, 1]\): a cluster is linked when the share is above it. For method = "jaccard", \(\theta\) in \((0, 1]\): two clusters can be linked when their Jaccard index is at least it. Higher values require more similar clusters and create more distinct dynamic clusters. Required.

similarity_type

"complete" or "partial", see the description. Required.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), says which rule is applied.

Value

The list of graphs, with the same names, where nodes have a new column dynamic_{cluster_id} (e.g. dynamic_cluster_leiden, with identifiers "cl_1", "cl_2"...) and edges the columns dynamic_{cluster_id}_from, dynamic_{cluster_id}_to and dynamic_{cluster_id} (missing for edges between clusters).

Details

Which windows? The rules need nodes present in successive windows. In a network of documents (e.g. bibliographic coupling), each document has a single date, so windows that do not overlap (window_step equal to time_window, the default of build_dynamic_networks()) share no node and no cluster can be matched: the windows must overlap (window_step smaller than time_window). Non-overlapping windows work when nodes persist over time, as cited references (co-citation), authors or journals do; two windows may still share no node when the literature changed completely.

Complete or partial? With overlapping windows, the network of window \(t\) loses the documents of the first years of window \(t-1\) and gains those of new years; in a growing literature, newcomers can be numerous. With "complete", a cluster that keeps all its past members but doubles with newcomers cannot inherit the identifier under the double majority, because its members coming from \(a\) are less than half of it: the cluster is considered new because its composition changed. With "partial", the newcomers are ignored and the same cluster keeps its identifier. Which one is right depends on what a cluster is taken to be: a group of documents (complete), or a structure that recruits new documents (partial).

Majority or Jaccard? The double majority is demanding and transparent: two clusters are the same if each is mostly made of the other, and the identifier is never ambiguous. The Jaccard matching is more flexible: with a low \(\theta\), it follows a cluster that splits (the largest piece, the best match, keeps the identifier) or that merges with another. Both use the nodes of consecutive windows only; compare them with merge_diagnostics().

What the rules do not do. Clusters are compared only with the previous window: a cluster that vanishes for one window and comes back gets a new identifier. Splits and merges are not recorded as such: one part keeps the identifier, the others are new. With a threshold close to its minimum, small fluctuations of the partition (a stochastic algorithm, a resolution change) may break or create continuities; it is good practice to compare the results for a few thresholds and seeds.

References

Greene D, Doyle D, Cunningham P (2010). “Tracking the Evolution of Communities in Dynamic Social Networks.” In 2010 International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining, 176–183. doi:10.1109/ASONAM.2010.17 .

Rosvall M, Bergstrom CT (2010). “Mapping Change in Large Networks.” PLoS ONE, 5(1), e8694. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0008694 .

See also

name_clusters() with name_dynamic_clusters = TRUE to label the dynamic clusters; networks_to_alluv() and plot_alluvial() to draw their evolution.

Examples

networks <- build_dynamic_networks(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  time_variable = "source_year",
  time_window = 10,
  method = "similarity",
  edges_threshold = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
#> Warning: The last window is shorter than the others.
#> ℹ The data end in "2013", but the last window ends in "2014".
networks <- add_clusters(
  networks,
  clustering_method = "leiden",
  objective_function = "modularity",
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)

networks <- merge_dynamic_clusters(
  networks,
  cluster_id = "cluster_leiden",
  node_id = "source_id",
  method = "majority",
  threshold_similarity = 0.51,
  similarity_type = "partial"
)
#> ℹ Linking clusters across windows with the "majority" rule: a cluster inherits
#>   the identifier of a past cluster when more than 0.51 of the nodes of each go
#>   to / come from the other (double majority). The comparison counts the nodes
#>   present in both windows only (`similarity_type` = "partial").
#> Warning: 3 pairs of consecutive windows share no node: their clusters cannot be matched.
#> ℹ Clusters are matched through the nodes they share. In a network of documents
#>   (coupling), each node has one date: the windows must overlap (`window_step`
#>   smaller than `time_window` in `build_dynamic_networks()`). If windows already
#>   overlap, the nodes may have changed completely, or the threshold may leave a
#>   window without edges.
networks[[2]]

  networks,

  similarity_type = "partial"
)
